thread:
sasha: heads up — noticed major chart slowdowns in the canary (EU) after today's console rollout. charts hang ~1.5s on initial open, CPU spike on main thread.
kevin: any telemetry/size blips? bundle size jump?
sasha: yep, sourcemap shows a 400KB increase in the main chunk. seems like the chart renderer chunk is getting pulled synchronously now. suspect dynamic import path resolution regressed in the splitter plugin.
kevin: ok — can you paste a quick repro? stacktrace or repro route?
sasha: repro:
```
open /dashboards/org/123/metrics -> clicks "View series" -> immediate freeze
perf: main thread flame shows blocking at ChartRenderer.mount -> renderLargeSeries
```
maria: temporary rollback to previous canary will stop user impact. also consider deferring heavy renderer with `import()` + placeholder.
jess: fwiw routing change from yesterday makes `/dashboards/*` request the detailed-metrics route by default which returns full time-series for up to 60s. that + renderer sync parse explains the pause. should we enforce default quota sampling on that route?
rahul: proposed fix:
- server-side: apply sampling/quota at REST layer (return summary + continuation stream)
- client-side: lazy-load renderer + incremental hydration (stream chunks into worker)
I can open a small PR for client lazy-load + worker fallback.
sasha: sounds good. +1 to server quota too, we can't rely on client only.
deploy-bot: deploy 1769999015 started by @rahul — attaching PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/3184
kevin: after PR lands, let's run quick canary with synthetic slow-device profiles. also add telemetry tags: `chart_load_path` and `series_count` so we can correlate.
maria: I'll rollback canary to previous build for now and file a postmortem.
sasha: thanks — adding a short repro gist and perf trace in the ticket.
